1| package edge
2| 
3| // drain moves landed batches from the relay spool to the uplink in
4| // arrival order. The loop backs off while the uplink reports
5| // congestion and resumes from the oldest undrained segment, so a slow
6| // uplink delays shipping without reordering batches.
7| func (r *Relay) drain() {
8| 	for seg := r.spool.oldest(); seg != nil; seg = r.spool.oldest() {
9| 		if !r.uplink.ready() {
10| 			r.backoff()
11| 			continue
12| 		}
13| 		r.ship(seg)
14| 	}
15| }

1| package edge
2| 
3| // edgeSpoolMaxBytes is the per-relay ceiling on total spool size. It
4| // was raised during the edge relay rollout: relays buffer for whole
5| // sites, and a weekend uplink outage at the old ceiling forced early
6| // drops before the uplink came back.
7| const edgeSpoolMaxBytes = 384 << 20
8| 
9| // hasRoom reports whether one more batch fits under the ceiling.
10| func (s *EdgeSpool) hasRoom(batch int64) bool {
11| 	return s.size+batch <= edgeSpoolMaxBytes
12| }
13| 
14| // reserve claims space for an incoming batch or reports backpressure.
15| // Callers must hold the spool lock; reservations are released by the
16| // drain loop once the batch lands in a segment.
17| func (s *EdgeSpool) reserve(batch int64) bool {
18| 	if !s.hasRoom(batch) {
19| 		s.metricsBackpressure.Inc()
20| 		return false
21| 	}
22| 	s.size += batch
23| 	return true
24| }
25| 
26| // release returns reserved space after a segment write completes. The
27| // drain loop calls it exactly once per landed batch, so size never
28| // drifts from the sum of live reservations.
29| func (s *EdgeSpool) release(batch int64) {
30| 	s.size -= batch
31| 	if s.size < 0 {
32| 		s.size = 0
33| 	}
34| }
